learn.explainer: Zero-click attacks target a device without requiring the user to take an action such as opening a link. The item describes such attacks against iOS and Android users visiting compromised or fake sites.
An underwater drone is an uncrewed vehicle designed to operate underwater. The item describes France’s contract to develop an operational demonstrator of a large oceangoing version.
Negotiations are discussions between parties seeking to address a dispute or reach an agreement. The item says Iran–US negotiations are continuing amid the prospect of a new escalation.

analysis.headline: Security, military capability, and political signals
paragraphs: The top stories span cyber risk, military technology, and political interpretation. The mobile watering hole report describes attacks through compromised or impersonating sites, while the LLMjacking item describes fraudulent cloud charges. Both make exposure and resource use relevant concerns, though the snippets do not establish a shared actor or campaign.

The Iran and Indonesia stories show how political messages and online tactics appear in the wider conflict environment. Ghalibaf endorses a claim about US voters, while the recruitment article compares Russian social-media tactics with scam-center methods. These reports suggest analysts should distinguish attributed claims from independently established details.

France’s planned underwater-drone demonstrator and the World War II account offer different views of military capability and support. Together, the stories underline the value of tracking both technical developments and human context. Watch for further detail on mobile exposure, recruitment tactics, and the capabilities described in the French contract.
takeaways: Review mobile exposure and cloud usage alongside conventional vulnerability checks.
Separate reported political claims from confirmed details when assessing conflict narratives.
Track both emerging military systems and the human context of operations.
